title: Genes or Surroundings? Moving Organisms to Find Out
endLine: Share one garden or swap homes to separate genes from surroundings.

scenes.tts: Plants on a mountain slope often look different from lowland relatives. Are those differences written in their genes, or shaped by where they grow? Watching them in place cannot tell.
scenes.caption: Plants on a mountain slope often look different from lowland relatives. Are those differences written in their genes, or shaped by where they grow? Watching them in place cannot tell.
scenes.visual: A schematic mountain slope fills most of the frame height, with warm-toned lowland plants on the left and distinct cool-toned highland plants on the right swaying gently in drifting air motes. Before the question is spoken, arrows rise from both sites toward a bold label: 'Genes or surroundings?'.
scenes.narration: Plants on a mountain slope often look different from lowland relatives. Are those differences written in their genes, or shaped by where they grow? Watching them in place cannot tell.

scenes.visual: The schematic mountain slope continues slow ambient motion as a high-contrast title fades in and holds briefly: 'Genes or Surroundings? Moving Organisms to Find Out'.

scenes.tts: To separate them, raise both populations in one shared environment, a common garden. Any difference that persists there supports an inherited basis. If they grow alike, the difference likely came from surroundings. Inherited variation within one population does not show that two populations differ genetically.
scenes.caption: To separate them, raise both populations in one shared environment, a common garden. Any difference that persists there supports an inherited basis. If they grow alike, the difference likely came from surroundings. Inherited variation within one population does not show that two populations differ genetically.
scenes.visual: Seeds drift from both ends of the mountain slope into one central shared plot labelled 'Common garden' (schematic). Uniform sun and rain icons pulse above it as two schematic outcomes animate in place: plants staying different ('Inherited basis') versus growing alike ('Surroundings'). A brief tag notes 'Within ≠ between populations'.
scenes.narration: To separate them, raise both populations in one shared environment, a common garden. Any difference that persists there supports an inherited basis. If they grow alike, the difference likely came from surroundings. Inherited variation within one population does not show that two populations differ genetically.

scenes.tts: Next, move organisms both ways between home sites in a reciprocal transplant, keeping controls at home. Then you measure how each group fares in both places. The core idea: match or swap environments to separate genes from surroundings.
scenes.caption: Next, move organisms both ways between home sites in a reciprocal transplant, keeping controls at home. Then you measure how each group fares in both places. The core idea: match or swap environments to separate genes from surroundings.
scenes.visual: The central plot splits into two active gardens directly on the lowland and highland slopes (schematic). Curved glowing arrows move plants both ways between sites while local controls stay rooted at home. Schematic performance gauges rise smoothly beside each plot as the core rule banner appears briefly.
scenes.narration: Next, move organisms both ways between home sites in a reciprocal transplant, keeping controls at home. Then you measure how each group fares in both places. The core idea: match or swap environments to separate genes from surroundings.

scenes.tts: With animals, swap parents instead of soil, a method called cross-fostering. Soon after laying, swap eggs between deep-beaked and shallow-beaked pairs, leaving other clutches at home. Measure chicks as adults. Predict: if genes alone drive beak depth, how should chicks match genetic and foster parents?
scenes.caption: With animals, swap parents instead of soil, a method called cross-fostering. Soon after laying, swap eggs between deep-beaked and shallow-beaked pairs, leaving other clutches at home. Measure chicks as adults. Predict: if genes alone drive beak depth, how should chicks match genetic and foster parents?
scenes.visual: The view pans smoothly up from the slope into two schematic nests in valley trees: deep-beaked parents on the left, shallow-beaked parents on the right, plus a control nest untouched. Eggs arc between the two nests and hatch into adult silhouettes. Below, two empty schematic scatter axes appear — 'Genetic parents' and 'Foster parents' — with pulsing question marks.
scenes.narration: With animals, swap parents instead of soil, a method called cross-fostering. Soon after laying, swap eggs between deep-beaked and shallow-beaked pairs, leaving other clutches at home. Measure chicks as adults. Predict: if genes alone drive beak depth, how should chicks match genetic and foster parents?

scenes.visual: Both empty schematic axes ('Genetic parents' and 'Foster parents') stay on screen beneath the prompt 'Genes alone: which slope rises?' while faint data points pulse gently during the thinking pause.

scenes.tts: If genes alone matter, the genetic-parent slope is positive while the foster-parent slope sits near zero. If rearing alone matters, those slopes reverse. If both contribute, both slopes are positive. Comparing them, with uncertainty, shows roughly how much each matters.
scenes.caption: If genes alone matter, the genetic-parent slope is positive while the foster-parent slope sits near zero. If rearing alone matters, those slopes reverse. If both contribute, both slopes are positive. Comparing them, with uncertainty, shows roughly how much each matters.
scenes.visual: On the same two schematic axes, a steep positive line draws onto 'Genetic parents' while 'Foster parents' draws flat near zero ('Genes only'). The two lines smoothly swap tilt ('Rearing only'). Finally, both tilt upward with shaded uncertainty bands ('Both contribute').
scenes.narration: If genes alone matter, the genetic-parent slope is positive while the foster-parent slope sits near zero. If rearing alone matters, those slopes reverse. If both contribute, both slopes are positive. Comparing them, with uncertainty, shows roughly how much each matters.

scenes.tts: Swaps still have limits, because early environments linger. Bird eggs are swapped after laying, so effects of the mother through the egg remain. Foster nests still differ in territory and food. In mice, cross-fostering pups controls nursing, not prenatal exposure; controlling the uterus requires transferring embryos.
scenes.caption: Swaps still have limits, because early environments linger. Bird eggs are swapped after laying, so effects of the mother through the egg remain. Foster nests still differ in territory and food. In mice, cross-fostering pups controls nursing, not prenatal exposure; controlling the uterus requires transferring embryos.
scenes.visual: Zooming toward a schematic egg in the foster nest highlights a glowing maternal-effect rim ('Egg effect remains'), while differing food silhouettes drift around the two nests ('Territory & food differ'). A clean schematic panel beside the nest shifts from a swapped newborn mouse pup ('Controls nursing') back to an embryo transferred into an unexposed female ('Controls uterus').
scenes.narration: Swaps still have limits, because early environments linger. Bird eggs are swapped after laying, so effects of the mother through the egg remain. Foster nests still differ in territory and food. In mice, cross-fostering pups controls nursing, not prenatal exposure; controlling the uterus requires transferring embryos.

scenes.tts: Guard against bias: start groups under matching conditions and assign them at random. A finch swap on one island belongs to that island and year; different seeds can shift it. And elevation changes many conditions at once, so temperature cannot be separated from the rest.
scenes.caption: Guard against bias: start groups under matching conditions and assign them at random. A finch swap on one island belongs to that island and year; different seeds can shift it. And elevation changes many conditions at once, so temperature cannot be separated from the rest.
scenes.visual: Returning to the mountain slope, a schematic starting tray shows uniform individuals split at random into plots ('Equal start, random split'). A changing seasonal seed icon passes over the valley over a small finch nest ('One island, one year'). Along the slope, thermometer, rain, and wind icons climb together ('Elevation mixes factors').
scenes.narration: Guard against bias: start groups under matching conditions and assign them at random. A finch swap on one island belongs to that island and year; different seeds can shift it. And elevation changes many conditions at once, so temperature cannot be separated from the rest.

scenes.tts: Even with those limits, transplants tested what sets species' ranges. A niche is where long-run lambda, the yearly births-and-deaths growth factor, stays at least one without immigrants. Amy Angert and Douglas Schemske grew two California monkeyflowers: low-elevation Mimulus cardinalis and high-elevation Mimulus lewisii. In gardens inside and beyond each range, both had zero or near-zero fitness past their limits.
scenes.caption: Even with those limits, transplants tested what sets species' ranges. A niche is where long-run λ, the yearly births-and-deaths growth factor, stays at least 1 without immigrants. Amy Angert and Douglas Schemske grew two California monkeyflowers: low-elevation Mimulus cardinalis and high-elevation Mimulus lewisii. In gardens inside and beyond each range, both had zero or near-zero fitness past their limits.
scenes.visual: Above the carried mountain slope, the formula 'N_next = λ · N + I' and the condition 'Niche: long-run λ ≥ 1 (I = 0)' appear as spoken. Then red-flowered Mimulus cardinalis grows in lowland gardens and drops to zero or near-zero schematic fitness bars above its upper limit, while pink-violet Mimulus lewisii grows in highland gardens and drops to near-zero below its lower limit. Label: 'Angert & Schemske'.
scenes.narration: Even with those limits, transplants tested what sets species' ranges. A niche is where long-run λ, the yearly births-and-deaths growth factor, stays at least 1 without immigrants. Amy Angert and Douglas Schemske grew two California monkeyflowers: low-elevation Mimulus cardinalis and high-elevation Mimulus lewisii. In gardens inside and beyond each range, both had zero or near-zero fitness past their limits.

scenes.tts: That fits niche limits. In 2014, Anna Hargreaves, Karen Samis and Christopher Eckert pooled one hundred eleven beyond-range transplant tests. In three quarters, performance fell beyond the edge. In forty-six percent, the range limit sat at a niche limit.
scenes.caption: That fits niche limits. In 2014, Anna Hargreaves, Karen Samis and Christopher Eckert pooled 111 beyond-range transplant tests. In three quarters, performance fell beyond the edge. In 46%, the range limit sat at a niche limit.
scenes.visual: The single slope zooms out into a schematic grid of 111 transplant sites across range edges (labelled 'Hargreaves, Samis & Eckert, 2014'); three quarters dim downward, and the first computed bar draws to 46% ('Niche limit').
scenes.narration: That fits niche limits. In 2014, Anna Hargreaves, Karen Samis and Christopher Eckert pooled 111 beyond-range transplant tests. In three quarters, performance fell beyond the edge. In 46%, the range limit sat at a niche limit.

scenes.tts: Twenty-six percent, mostly latitudinal or longitudinal, sustained themselves beyond the range, fitting dispersal limitation: suitable places never reached. Twenty-three percent, all at elevation limits, were sinks: immigrants sustain them despite lambda below one. The shares do not add to one hundred percent. Control or swap environments, and genes separate from surroundings.
scenes.caption: 26%, mostly latitudinal or longitudinal, sustained themselves beyond the range, fitting dispersal limitation: suitable places never reached. 23%, all at elevation limits, were sinks: immigrants sustain them despite λ below 1. The shares do not add to 100%. Control or swap environments, and genes separate from surroundings.
scenes.visual: Two more computed horizontal bars join 46% on the 0 to 100% scale: 26% ('Dispersal limitation: λ ≥ 1, N = 0') and 23% ('Elevation sinks: λ < 1, I > 0'), with a clear note 'Shares do not add to 100%'. A gentle arrow loops back to the carried mountain slope as its lowland and highland gardens glow cleanly.
scenes.narration: 26%, mostly latitudinal or longitudinal, sustained themselves beyond the range, fitting dispersal limitation: suitable places never reached. 23%, all at elevation limits, were sinks: immigrants sustain them despite λ below 1.
